## {background-image="images/slides-final/slide-01.png" background-size="contain" background-repeat="no-repeat" background-position="center" background-color="#ffffff"}

<p class="sr-only">Tensors for Machine Learning — from real data to modern models. Presenter: Ravi Kalia. Prepared by: Sebastian Laverde Chunza.</p>

## {background-image="images/slides-final/slide-02.png" background-size="contain" background-repeat="no-repeat" background-position="center" background-color="#ffffff"}

<p class="sr-only">The workshop idea: four cards show scalar, vector, matrix and tensor as 0D, 1D, 2D and ND arrays, each defined by its shape. The guiding question of the day: before operating, what does each axis represent?</p>

## {background-image="images/slides-final/slide-03.png" background-size="contain" background-repeat="no-repeat" background-position="center" background-color="#ffffff"}

<p class="sr-only">Real data, real problems: four real datasets used throughout the workshop — handwritten digits, stained histology, California housing, and NYC taxi trips — each with the role it plays later.</p>

## {background-image="images/slides-final/slide-06.png" background-size="contain" background-repeat="no-repeat" background-position="center" background-color="#ffffff"}

<p class="sr-only">Map of factorizations: six matrix and tensor factorizations arranged on a ladder from LU through Cholesky, QR, SVD, Tucker and CP, each with one phrase describing what it buys.</p>

## {background-image="images/slides-final/slide-07.png" background-size="contain" background-repeat="no-repeat" background-position="center" background-color="#ffffff"}

<p class="sr-only">What does a factorization give you? A four-step diagram — number, polynomial, matrix, tensor — shows that factorizing reveals useful structure rather than just rewriting an expression.</p>
